description: Heat-advisory action library (Phase 6). Built by advisory/library.py from sources/phase6_candidate_actions.json; do not edit by hand.

labels.imd_style: IMD-style, adjusted for area-average data; not an official IMD warning
labels.precedent: Precedent from Ahmedabad's Heat Action Plan (2019 update), not Delhi policy
labels.clinical: Clinical and health-system guidance quoted from official health documents, for trained health workers only. Members of the public: call 108 or 102.

excluded.WHO_ENERGY_UTILITIES_SUSPEND_DISCONNECTI: low confidence: international practice (WHO/WMO), not a Delhi instruction
excluded.WHO_ENERGY_PHILADELPHIA_HALT_SERVICE_SUS: low confidence: a Philadelphia (USA) example, not a Delhi instruction

actions.text: All BEE star-labelled room air conditioners must have a default temperature setting of 24 °C from 1 Jan 2020
actions.trigger: Standing manufacturer requirement; not tied to any heat alert

source.text: default setting has been made mandatory from Jan 1, 2020 for all room air conditioners covered under the ambit of BEE star-labelling program

actions.notes: Image-only PDF (no text layer): quote read from the page image and checked by eye. This is a PIB press release (Ministry of Power, 6 Jan 2020) that quotes the BEE notification; it is not the Gazette notification itself. It binds manufacturers/sellers, not consumers, so it is not an advisory to citizens. The release's phrase 'The 24°C default setting' is printed with a superscript degree sign, so the quote starts after it. Conflicts with Delhi HAP 'run the AC at 25 degree' (DELHI_HAP_2025 p.53).

actions.notes: Image-only PDF (no text layer): quote read from the page image and checked by eye. CEA Chief Electrical Inspectorate Division advisory addressed to 'MDs of all DISCOMs / All Electricity Consumers', subject 'Advisory on safe and judicious use of electricity in view of El Nino conditions or otherwise'. No date is visible on the scanned pages. National, not Delhi-specific, but it names fire/AC-blast incidents in Delhi. actions.notes: Design principle supporting tiered actions. PDF page 65 (printed 49).

actions.text: Visit at-risk adults at least twice a day and watch for heat exhaustion or heatstroke

source.text: Visit adults at risk at least twice a day and watch them closely for signs of heat exhaustion or heatstroke.

actions.notes: Adapted by WHO/WMO from US CDC advice (Box 2). PDF page 68 (printed 52).

actions.text: Encourage workers to drink about one cup of cool water every 15–20 minutes

source.text: Encourage workers to drink plenty of water – about one cup of cool water every 15 to 20 minutes, even if they are not thirsty

actions.notes: Adapted from OSHA (Box 7). PDF page 72 (printed 56).
